title: #26. The Battle Of Uhud Part 2
arabic:
اَعُوْذُ بِاللهِ مِنَّ الشِّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيْمِ۝

بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَانِ الرَّحِيْمَ۝

اَلْحَمْدُ لله ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلى سَيِّدِنَا محمد وَعَلَى اَلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ وَسَلِّمْ تَسْلِيْمًا كَثِيْرا السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته

وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ بِإِذْنِهِ ۖ وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ بِإِذْنِهِ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا فَشِلْتُمْ وَتَنَازَعْتُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ وَعَصَيْتُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا أَرَاكُمْ مَا تُحِبُّونَ۝

مِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيَا وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الْآخِرَةَ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَفَا عَنْكُمْۗ وَاللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ۝

لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَوْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ۝

لا اله الا الله أُعْلُوْا هُبَلْ اَلله اَعْلى وَ اَجَلْ لَنَا الْعُزَّى وَلَاعُزَّى لَكُمْ اَللهُ مَوْلَانَا وَلَامَوْلَى لَكُمْ Allahعَزّوجَلّsays,

إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ وَلَا تَلْوُونَ عَلَىٰ أَحَدٍ وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ فِي أُخْرَاكُمْ وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ فِي أُخْرَاكُمْ فَأَثَابَكُمْ غَمًّا بِغَمٍّ لِكَيْلَا تَحْزَنُوا

لِكَيْلَا تَحْزَنُوا عَلَىٰ مَا فَاتَكُمْ وَلَا مَا أَصَابَكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ۝

إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْا مِنْكُمْ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ إِنَّمَا اسْتَزَلَّهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ إِنَّمَا اسْتَزَلَّهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ بِبَعْضِ مَا كَسَبُوا ۖ

وَلَقَدْ عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ۝

قُلْ إِنَّ الْأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ لِلَّهِ يُخْفُونَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ مَا لَا يُبْدُونَ لَكَ يَقُولُونَ لَوْ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ مَا قُتِلْنَا هَاهُنَا

قُلْ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ لَبَرَزَ الَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَتْلُ إِلَىٰ مَضَاجِعِهِمْ ۖ وَلِيَبْتَلِيَ اللَّهُ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ ۗ

وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ۝

إنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ مَا زِلْتُ بَعْدَ ذَالِكْ تَصَدَّقْ وَ أعتق الرَّقَابْ وَاَصُوْمْ فِيْ سَبِيْلِ الله لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَوْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ۝

مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ رِجَالٌ صَدَقُوا مَا عَاهَدُوا اللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ ۖ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَضَىٰ نَحْبَهُ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْتَظِرُ ۖ اَبْشِرْ بِالْجَنَّةْ

صَلَّى الله عَلى سَيَّدِنَا محمد وَعَلى اَلِهِ وَ صَحْبِهِ وَسَلِّمْ وَالسلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته
english:
The Life of Muhammadﷺ, The Madinan Period, Volume 1 By Imam Anwar Al_Awlaki, Rasool Allah ﷺ held a sword in his hand, and he asked the Sahabah(صحابه), who will take this sword from me.

So, the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم volunteered.

But then Rasool Allah ﷺ said, Who will take this sword along with its rights.

So, this sword you don't just take it.

I'm not just giving it to you, but this sword has some rights.

So, the Sahabah(صحابه) asked Rasool Allah ﷺ; What are the rights of this sword.

Rasool Allah ﷺ said; For you to strike the enemy with it, until it bends.

So, now the Sahabah(صحابه) were giving it a second thought, I mean, taking a sword until you bend it.

But Abu Dujana رضي الله عنه came forward and said, I will, O Rasool Allah ﷺ, I'm going to take it, I'm up for that challenge,  I'll hit the enemy with it, until I bend it,

I'm going to bend that piece of steel.

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ gives it to him.

Ibn Is'haaq(إبن اسحاق) says, When he took the sword from Rasool Allah ﷺ, he took out the red headband and put it on.

He then began strutting about between the two lines.

Abu Dujana(ابودجانه), when he would fight, he would put on a red headband.

That's the sign that he's going to war.

So, he pulls up that red headband puts it on, and then he starts to march in front of the army with pride.

He's emanating this pride you can feel the strength in his walk, strutting in front of the enemy.

Rasool Allah ﷺ said; That is a way of walking that Allah dislikes, except in circumstances like this.

Allahعَزّوجَلّ does not like this way of walking, but in this particular situation, Allah does like it.

A Muslim is not supposed to be arrogant, so that's why we walk with humbleness, we walk with humbleness.

Rasool Allah ﷺ would walk with humbleness, now we don't want this to be misunderstood as walking with weakness, the humbleness is something and weakness is something else.

Rasool Allah ﷺ when he would walk, you can see the strength in Rasool Allah ﷺ in the way he would walk.

Ali Ibn Abi Talib(علي ابن ابي طالب) said; As if he's coming down a hill.

So, it's like firmness in walking.

So, that's different than, we shouldn't think that being humble is that you're walking with weakness.

But here Abu Dujana(ابو دجانه) is walking with pride, Khuayalaa(خُيَّلَآءْ), and that's not something that Allah likes, but this is done in front of the enemy.

And that's why Allahعَزّوجَلّ likes in this particular situation.

Imam Ahmad(اِمَامْ اَحْمَدْ) said: And he did take it, referring to the sword, that he did take it and cleaved a path with it, through the middle of the Polytheists.

In the middle of the Mushrikeen(مشركين) So, Abu Dujana(ابو دجانه) takes this sword, in order to bend it, he wrecks havoc in the ranks of the enemy and splits up their ranks,

he cleaved the path with it, through the middle of Al-Mushrikeen(ألمشركين).

Abdullah Bin Zubair(عبدالله بن الزبير), he narrates to us a story of a scene that he witnessed on the day of Uhud(أحَد).

He said, Every man he met Abu Dujana(ابو دجانه) killed.

Among the Mushrikeen(مشركين) there was man, who executed every man he wounded.

Meaning this man he doesn't spare the life of anyone.

If he meets a Muslim, A Muslim is dead.

This man and Abu Dujana(دجانه) came ever closer to one another.

And I pray to Allah to bring them together.

And they did meet.

They exchanged a couple of blows, the Mushrik(مشرك) then struck at Abu Dujana(ابو دجانه), who fended off the blow with his shield which trap the man sword,

then Abu Dujana(ابو دجانه) struck and killed him.

Ka'ab Ibn Malik(كعب ابن مالك) narrates a similar story, Allah Ho Alam(الله اعلم) if it's talking about the same person it could be or it could be somebody else.

Ka'ab Ibn Malik(كعب ابن مالك) said, I then saw one Mushrik(مشرك) heavily armored was striking the Muslims hard and saying Come on, you sheep gathering for slaughter.

But then I saw one Muslim fully armored, I mean he doesn't know this Muslim was, his armory was covering the face.

But then I saw one Muslim fully armored waiting for him, and I went on over behind him and began comparing the Muslim with the Mushrik(مشرك).

So, Ka'ab Ibn Malik(كعب ابن مالك) here saw these two men and he was sizing them up.

He says the latter was better in equipment and form, meaning the Mushrik(مشرك) was bigger and stronger and he also had better equipment, so you would expect that the Mushrik(مشرك) would win.

I kept on waiting until they met.

The Muslim then struck the unbeliever a blow with his sword on his shoulder, the sword came right down through, to his thigh.

So, he struck the Mushrik(مشرك) on the shoulder and the sword went through tearing apart his torso until it came out from under his thigh, cutting him into two.

Ka'ab Ibn Malik(كعب ابن مالك) said: Then the Muslim uncovered his face and said, What about that Ka'ab(كعب)? I'm Abu Dujana(ابودجانه).

So, Abu Dujana(ابودجانه) knew that Ka'ab(كعب) was watching and watching this match.

So, when the match was over, Abu Dujana(ابودجانه) uncovers his faces, and says, What about that Ka'ab(كعب), I'm Abu Dujana(ابودجانه).

He was a proud man, and he has every right to be proud.

The Muslims were winning, and the enemy was fleeing the battle ground.

And the Sahabah(صحابه) said, We could see, the women of Arabia used to put this jewelry on their feet.

So, they would say that we would see that jewelry on their feet because they're tucking up their clothes to run away.

So, that's it. The enemy was showing the Muslims, their backs.

Bannu Abd-Ad-Daar(بنوعبدالدار) were the ones, who had the responsibility of holding the standard of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ).

And this was part of the Division of authorities that existed in Quraish(قُرَيْشْ), one family would take care of feeding the pilgrims, one family had the key to Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه),

one family had the key to An-Nadwa(ألندوى), the sort of the Parliament of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) and one family, they held the banners of war.

So, this family was Bannu Abd-Ad-Daar(بنوعبدالدار), they were the ones responsible for it on Badr(بدر) and they are also responsible for it, on Uhud(أحَد).

And I mean to show you the importance of the standard.

You know, because probably due to modern warfare, we don't really understand what's the significance of a banner.

That was the rallying point, that was the indication to the soldier that we're still in the fight and my army is here.

Without the banner, the soldier is not going to fight anymore.

If the banner falls down, that means that we have lost the war, and it's time for me to run away.

So to show the significance of this banner issue, Abu Sufiyan(ابوسفيان) told Bannu Abd-Ad-Daar(بنوعبدالدار); You were incharge of our banner at the Battle of Badr(بدر).

And you saw what happened to us, men will only fight for their flags.

If once, they are lost, they withdraw, either take care of our banner for us or give it over to us and we will relieve you of it.

So, this angered them and said we give over our banner to you.

You will learn tomorrow when we meet and in battle, how we will behave.

So, he charged them up.

And that was the response Abu Sufiyan(ابوسفيان) wanted.

So they fought under their banner well.

I mean, Bannu Abd-Ad-Daar(بنوعبدالدار) they lost seven of their men one after the other.

One would hold the banner that he would be killed.

The second would come in line take it over, he would be killed, third, Seven of their men were killed carrying the banner and then one of their slaves, his name is Sawaab(ثواب)

Abyssinian slave, he took hold of it and his arms were severed, and he was still trying to hug the banner and then he would say, Aazart(أعذرْتْ)

Have I done my part and he couldn't pronounce the Za(ز), it was Azart( آعزرت) but his Arabic wasn't perfect, so he said: Aazart(أعذرْتْ).

Anyway so after that the banner just fell down and they left it on the ground, and that is when Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) started to flee the battle ground.

So, they were defeated, they lost And Allahعَزّوجَلّ said, And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission.

So, even according to Qur'an, the Muslims have won the battle of Uhud(أحَد) initially.

But the tides were turning.

The archers, who were instructed by Rasool Allah ﷺ to remain on the hill not to move, if you see us winning, Do not come down until I tell you,

if you see us losing and vultures picking off our bodies eating from our bodies, Do not come down until I tell you, very explicit, clear, instructions from Rasool Allah ﷺ.

Now in the heat of battle when the emotions take over, sometimes the mind is obscured.

So, what happened is, when the archers saw that the Muslims were now gathering booty, Al-Ghanaem(ألغنائم), they wanted to go down and join.

But their Ameer(امير) Abdullah Bin Jubair(عبدالله بن جبير), he said, Don't you remember the instructions of Rasool Allah ﷺ, that we shouldn't come down, until he tells us so.

They said the battle is over and they left.

So, out of the 50 archers, 40 of them defected.

We're going to call this defection because that's what it is.

They have disobeyed the order of Rasool Allah ﷺ, and this is a serious thing in warfare, to disobey the commander.

Or not defected, we should call it, it was mutiny, so they left their post.

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) was the head of the cavalry of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ).

He and Ikrimah Bin Abi Jahal(عكرمه بن ابي جهل).

When they detected the weak point, that was exposed they immediately took advantage of that, and outflanked the Muslim army.

And because the Muslims were not expecting that, and they were taken by surprise.

It was a chaotic state for the Muslims, and when the army of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) saw that they attacked from the other side, so now the Muslims were sandwiched,

they were attacked from both sides from the front and from the rear.

And this disoriented the Muslim soldiers because they are fighting now in both direction and the ranks would became disorganized, they were not lined up properly as they should.

And that is when the Muslims were defeated.

And that is when they were being killed, and they were falling one after the other.

It is said that only 12 men remained around Rasool Allah ﷺ.

Allahعزوجل says; Allah has certainly fulfilled His promise to you, when you were killing them by His permission, until the time when you lost courage

and fell to disputing about the order given by the prophet and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love, I mean, victory.

After among you are some, who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter.

Abdullah Bin Masood(عبدالله بن مسعود) said, I didn't know that there were some of us who loved and desire this world, until this Ayah(آية) was revealed.

So, Qur'an was exposing what was in the hearts this is how Qur'an writes history, it doesn't only take the outside, but it also takes the inner dimension of the soul.

Then Allah says, Then he turned you back from them defeated, that He might test you.

And he has already forgiven you.

And Allah is the possessor of bounty for the believers.

So, Allah tested the believers with victory on Badr(بدر) and He is now testing them with the defeat on Uhud(أحَد).

It's all test from Allahعَزّوجَلّ.

Ibn Is'haqq(اِبْنِ اِسْحَاقْ) said, the Muslim ranks broke and the enemy gained advantage over them.

It was the day of trial and testing, in which Allah honored someone with martyrdom.

At last the enemy broke through to Rasool Allah ﷺ, he was hit with a rock and fell on his side, breaking his front teeth, slashing his face and splitting his lips.

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ himself was injured in the Battle of Uhud(أحَد).

In Al-Bukhari(البخاريْ) it says that Fatima(فاطمه) was the one, who was washing him, and Ali(علي) poured the water from the shield.

So, Ali(علي) was pouring the water and Fatima(فاطمه) was washing the wounds.

When Fatima(فاطمه) saw that the water was only increasing the blood flow She took a piece of matting and she set fire to it and then attach it to the wound.

So, over here you have, it is ashes, and it's also hot ashes are very dry and it would absorb the water from the wound and make it dry and that would prevent the blood from flowing.

And It's also hot so it would probably disinfect the wound.

This is mentioned in Bukhari(بخاريْ), it says that the blood seized flowing and his front tooth was broken that day his face was wounded and his helmet was crushed onto his head.

It was Ibn Qamiyah(إبن قميه) who shot Rasool Allah ﷺ at the cheek and it was Utba Bin Abi Waqas(عتبةبن ابي وقاص), who hit the lip and lower tooth of Rasool Allah ﷺ.

Abdur Razzaq(عبدالرزاق) says, The Messenger of Allah spoke a curse against Utba Bin Abi Waqas(عتبة بن ابي وقاص) saying; O Allah may change not come to him.

So, that he does die as an unbeliever.

Ibn Kathir(اِبْنِ كَثِيْر) commented and no change did come over him so that he did die as an unbeliever bound for hellfire.

So, what was the reaction to this defeat, Rasool Allah ﷺ as narrated by Anas Ibn Malik رضي الله عنه, he said, While Rasool was wiping the blood off his face,

He said, How could any people prosper, Who struck their prophet and broke his front teeth?

While he called people to Allah.

How could these people prosper?

How could they succeed?

When they do this to the Prophet who's calling them to Allahعَزّوجَلّ.

Allahعَزّوجَلّ revealed the Ayah(آية), Not for you, O Muhammad(محمد) but for Allah is the decision whether He should cut them down or forgive them or punish them.

For indeed they are wrongdoers.

So, Allahعَزّوجَلّ is saying, The fate of these people is not up to you It's in the hands of Allahعَزّوجَلّ It is up to Allahعَزّوجَلّ to cut them down, or to forgive them, or to punish them.

They deserve punishment but if Allahعَزّوجَلّ wants to forgive them, it is up to Him.

So, this shows you that even Rasool Allah ﷺ does not control the fate of humanity.

It's all in the hands of Allahعَزّوجَلّ, Allahعَزّوجَلّ is the One, Who controls, who becomes Muslim and who doesn't and who should be punished and who shouldn't be punished.

So, if this right wasn't given to Rasool Allah ﷺ who are we to claim that right?

It's all in the hands of Allahعَزّوجَلّ.

Some of the Muslims, when they saw the defeat, and when they heard the rumor that Rasool Allah ﷺ was killed because this rumors spread like wildfire in the Muslim army that he was killed.

The origin of the rumor was that he was injured, but you know, in such a state, things could get blown out of proportion.

So, the rumor that was going around was that Rasool Allah ﷺ was in fact killed.

So, how did they react to that?

Well, some of them said, We'd better send an envoy to Abdullah Bin Obaeye(عبدالله بن ابيئ) and have him get us a truce from Abu Sufiyan(ابوسفيان).

People! Muhammad(محمد) has been killed, go back home before they get to you and kill you.

Here we have some Muslims, who are defeated, the defeat reached to their hearts.

And under the pressure of the moment, they thought that the best course of action was to go to Abdullah Bin Obaeye(عبدالله بن ابي), the Munafiq(منافق)

because he has good relations with Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) and to ask him to bring a truce.

And Ya'ani(يعني) Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله), The Battle of Uhud(أحَد), itself may not repeat but the reaction of the people can repeat in events that are similar.

So, sometimes you'd find that when Muslims are under pressure and when they feel that they could be defeated in battle, you can have some people who would now think well, why don't I go to the government's

and ask them to help me or why don't I go to the enemies of Allahعَزّوجَلّ and let's have a truce with them.

This is a sign of weakness.

But the Muslims, who had strong Eeman(ايمان) in their hearts, what was their reaction?

One of Al-Muhajiroon(المهاجرون) said that he passed by one of Al-Ansaar(ألأنصار) a man, who was covered in his own blood, He was soaked in his own blood and asked him.

Are you aware that Muhammad(محمد) has been killed.

The Ansaari(انصاري) responded if Muhammad(محمد) has been killed then he must have fulfilled his mission, so fight on for your religion.

Let's die as he died fighting for Islam.

So, these are Muslims, who cannot be defeated in their hearts, even if they're defeated on the battleground, defeat will never get into their spirit.

They will always have commitment and this is, what is called in Islam thabaat(ثبات) steadfast.

Never would such a Muslim try to negotiate with the enemy of Allahعَزّوجَلّ or ask the Munafiqeen(منافقين), to appeal and intercede for them.

Fine, if Rasool Allah ﷺ was killed, we're gonna die like he was.

And this is the steadfastness that we should learn from the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم.

The Muslims had to retreat, so Rasool Allah ﷺ was trying to organize that retreat, but retreats could be catastrophic if they are not commanded well.

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ wants to organize this retreat and to protect themselves while they are retreating.

So, the enemy now was gaining the upper hand and was attacking in full force and they were getting closer to Rasool Allah ﷺ.

So, Rasool Ullah asked, He said, Whoever will repel them, will be my companion in paradise.

I mean, that's how difficult the situation was, Rasool Ullah was promising paradise to the one, who will succeed in stopping the attacks of the kuffar(كفار) that were reaching him.

So, one of Al-Ansaar(الانصار) volunteered and he would fire his arrows at the enemy until he was killed.

So Rasool Allah ﷺ asks for a volunteer another time, another Ansari(انصاري) comes up, he's also killed and a third time, a third Ansaari(انصاري) would stand up

and then a fourth and the fifth and every time they're killed, so this in addition to the sacrifice of Al-Ansaar(الأنْصَار), can also show you the disastrous effect this attack of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) was having,

it was a strong attack, until seven of Al-Ansaar(الانصار) died under Rasool Allah ﷺ.

Allah u Akbar(الله اكبر).

Seven bodies, laying under the feet of Rasool Allah ﷺ, to defend him.

O Allah, If I meet the enemy then enable me to meet a strong fighter who will fight me and I will fight him and then give me victory over him

and enable me to kill him and take his Salb(سلب), take his armor.

Abdullah Bin Jahash(عبدالله بن جحش) said, Ameen(آمين) Sa'ad told him, it's now your turn to make Dua(دعا).

Abdullah Bin Jahash(عبدالله بن جحش) said, O Allah enabled me to meet a strong fighter who would fight me and I would fight him.

And then he would kill me and cut my nose and ear.

So, when I meet You, You will say why was your ear and nose cut, O Abdallah(عبدالله).?

I would say for you and your messenger.

And you would say, you are speaking the truth.

Sa'ad Ibn Abi Waqas(سعد ابن ابي وقاص) said: Ameen(آمين) Sa'ad(سعد) was narrating the story to his son.

And he said, Oh, my son, the Dua(دعا) of AbdAllah(عبدالله) was better than mine.

By the end of the day, I saw his nose and ear tied to a string.

Allah did accept the Dua(دعا) of Abdullah Bin Jahash(عبدالله بن جحش) and he did meet a strong man, who fought him and killed him and then, his body was mutilated, and his nose was cut and his ears were cut

and there they were tied in a string and Sa'ad(سعد) saw that string with his own eyes.

This Dua(دعا) shows that it is allowed to ask Allah to give you death, if it is in his path, if it is Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله) Another amazing story of a Shaheed(شهيد) was that of Abdullah Bin Haraam رضي الله عنه,

or actually I mentioned the story of Khaisamah(خيثمة), and this was narrated by Ibn Al-Qayyim(إبن قيم) in Zaad Al-Ma'ad(زاد المعاد).

Khaisamah(خيثمة) was an old man, but he still wanted to join and fight and we know that old men are excused.

Khaisamah(خيثمة), his son died as a Shaheed(شهيد) on Badr(بدر).

So, he said I missed the Battle of Badr(بدر) and I was so eager to join, but me and my son drew lots and he went and was awarded with martyrdom.

So, one of them stayed behind, so they cast lots, and it came out that Khaisamah(خيثمة) has to stay and his son has to go.

Khaisamah(خيثمة) then said, I saw him last night in my sleep.

He looked great and was enjoying the fruits of Jannah(جنة).

He told me come and be our companion in paradise.

I have found what Allah promise me to be true.

So, O Messenger of Allah, I swear to Allah, I am so eager to join him in Jannah(جنة) I am old and my bones are soft.

So, ask Allah, O Messenger of Allah to award me Shahadah(شهادة) and allow me to join Sa'ad(سعد) in Jannah(جنة).

Khaisamah(خيثمة) is saying, I'm getting old, I'm missing the train, I'm afraid that if I don't die as a Shaheed(شهيد) now I might end up dying on my bed.

So, O messenger of Allah make Dua(دعا) that I die as a Shaheed(شهيد).

I want to meet my son, I want to join him in Jannah(جنه).

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ did make Dua(دعا) for him and he did die as a shaheed رضي الله عنه.

Wahb Al-Muzani(وهب المزني), these are not from Madina, but they're from outside, from a tribe called Muzaina(مزينه).

He and his relative were shepherds and they came to Madina with their sheep and they came to find Madina empty.

They said, Where is everyone?

They said they went to fight with Rasool Allah ﷺ at the Battle of Uhud(أحد).

So, they left their sheep and they went to join the battle.

They came while the Muslims were winning, they joined in.

But then when the tides returning they carried on the fight, they didn't just join because the Muslims were winning, they were also fighting with the Muslims, when they were being defeated.

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ saw a group approaching them and he said, Who will take care of this group.

So, Al-Muzzani(المزني) said: I will, Wahb(وهب) said, I will.

So, he advances and attacks them.

And he pushes them back.

A second group comes in and Rasool Allah ﷺ asks for volunteers Al-Muzzani(المزني) goes again and volunteers and he stops them and pushes them back.

The third time, he also stands up so this time, Rasool Allah ﷺ said, Go and receive the glad tidings of Jannah(جنة) So, he went into fight, and he was throwing himself in the middle of this group,

and then he would come out and attack again and come out and attack again.

Rasool Allah ﷺ was watching that and he would say, O, Allah: Yarham(يرحم) O Allah have mercy on him.

Rasool Ullah was making Dua(دعا) for Wahb Al-Muzzani(وهب المزني) and he continued doing this until these swords shredded him and he was killed.

By the way, when they found his body, He had 20 injuries all of them were fatal injuries and Umar Bin Khattab رضي الله عنه said; that is the best death I could wish for.

That's how I want to die.

Look at those injuries and every one of them is fatal and he was still fighting.

Sa'ad Ibn Abi Waqas(سعد ابن ابي وقاص) after the Battle of Al-Qadisiyya(القادسيه) was approached by a man from Muzaina(مزينه), his name is Bilal(بلال)

because, one of his relatives didn't get his share of the booty.

So, they went to visit Sa'ad(سعد).

So, Sa'ad(سعد) asked this man he said, Are you a relative of Wahb Al-Muzzani(وهب المزني)?

He said: yes, I'm his nephew.

So, Sa'ad, said, and this is years later, this is 13 years later Sa'ad(سعد) is still remembering that day.

He said; On that day, when Rasool Allah ﷺ was asking for volunteers to go and stop this group.

It was your uncle who was attacking them all the time.

The third time, I went to join him because I wanted to receive the same reward that he would receive because I heard Rasool Allah ﷺ say, you receive the glad tidings of Jannah.

So, Sa'ad(سعد) said, I went with him and he mentioned how brave and courageous Wahb(وهب) was until, he was killed.

Sa'ad(سعد) said, No state of death would I love to meet Allah with more than the state of death of that was Al-Muzzani(المزني).

That's the best way to die.

Sa'ad(سعد) said; When he was killed after the battle was over.

I saw Rasool Allah ﷺ go and stand on top of his grave when they were digging it and waiting right there, until the burial was over, even though Rasool Allah ﷺ was exhausted.

Rasool Allah was injured and he was tired and he could barely stand up.

But he nevertheless stood up, on his grave, until he was buried.

And then Rasool Allah ﷺ said, may Allah be pleased with him because I am pleased with him.

O Allah, be pleased with him because I am pleased with him.

Amr Bin Jammooh(عمرو بن جموح) another Shaheed(شهيد).

Ibn Is'haaq(ابن اسحاق) narrates; My father related to me, he is mentioning this, in the book of Ibn Is'haaq(ابن اسحاق) My father related to me from elders of Bannu Salamah(بنوسلمه), who said;

Amr Bin Jammooh(عمرو بن جموح), was a man exceedingly lame.

He had four sons who fought battles like lions alongside the Messenger of Allah.

When it came time for the Battle of Uhud(أحَد).

They wanted to restrain Amr(عمرو) saying that Allah has excused him.

So, he went to Rasool Allah ﷺ and said, My sons want to restrain me from going to battle with you.

But by Allah, I want to step this lame foot of mine into Paradise.

Rasool Allah ﷺ told him it's not obliged to you to fight because you're lame, Aaraj(اعرج), you don't have to fight.

But then Rasool Allahﷺ told his sons, it is not your duty to restrain him, if he wants to fight let him go.

Allah might well grant him martyrdom and he did die as a Shaheed(شهيد).

So, we learn from this that even if a person is excused from fighting, it is allowed for him to fight. If it's not obligatory on him, he can still fight.

We know that the blind man has fought in battles, we know that lame men have fought in battles, we know that people who are have other diseases did fight in battle.

So, it's allowed for a person who is excused from fighting to join in and fight.

This also shows you how eager the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم were to die as Shaheeds(شهيد).

We'll stop here and carry on In Sha Allah Ta'ala(ان شاء الله تعالى) tomorrow with some other stories of Ash-Shuhadaa(الشهدآء)
